extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI): user-controlled 'name' query parameter is interpolated into a template string at app/main.py:38 and then passed to jinja2.Template(...).render() here. Because the user input is inserted into the template source before it is parsed, payloads such as '{{7*7}}' or attribute access expressions like '{{config.__class__.__init__.__globals__[...]}}' are evaluated by Jinja2, enabling remote code execution, information disclosure, and full server compromise.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS): the user-controlled 'name' query parameter is concatenated into an HTML string via f-string interpolation at app/main.py:38 without any HTML escaping, and the endpoint is declared with response_class=HTMLResponse (app/main.py:18) so the response is served as text/html. An attacker can supply a 'name' such as '<script>alert(document.cookie)</script>' and have it executed in the victim's browser, leading to session hijacking, credential theft, or account takeover.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: Hardcoded sensitive credential: SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN is assigned the literal value '5u93R53Cr3tT0k3n' at app/config.py:15 instead of being loaded from an environment variable or a secrets manager. Anyone with access to the source code, repository history, or built image can read this token and use it for authentication or API access. The inline 'FIXME' comment confirms this was intended to be replaced with os.getenv().

Hardcoded sensitive default value: SUPER_SECRET_NAME is assigned the literal 'John Ripper' at app/config.py:13. While the value itself is not a credential, it is named and treated as a 'super secret' but is committed to the repository in plaintext, exposing the intended secret-handling pattern and any private data it may contain. The inline 'FIXME' comment confirms this was intended to be replaced with os.getenv().

Security misconfiguration: FastAPI is constructed with debug=config.DEBUG (app/main.py:14). The shipped .env_temp file (line 3) sets DEBUG=True by default, which enables Starlette/Uvicorn debug mode and serves detailed tracebacks, internal variable values, and source paths on unhandled exceptions. This can leak stack traces, file paths, secrets in locals, and library versions to remote attackers.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
